{"content":{"id":2442,"headline":"Assessing a new technique to shrink liver tumors in dogs","tagline":"Help us learn more about this new technique that could shrink liver tumors in dogs!","description":"When liver tumors in dogs cannot be removed with surgery, treatment options are limited or non-existent. In humans, one of the standard treatments for those cases is transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), which eliminates the blood supply of the tumor and may decrease tumor size. The objectives of this study are to 1) describe the procedure of TACE using a novel treatment agent in a group of dogs with naturally-occurring liver cancer, and 2) evaluate the effect that liver TACE has on clinical signs, size and viability of the tumor.\r\n\r\nDemonstrating the feasibility and efficacy of liver TACE to improve clinical signs and decrease tumor size and volume can significantly advance our treatment of this difficult disease process, as current treatment options are limited and lack efficacy. Additionally, liver TACE is minimally invasive and provides many potential advantages over traditional surgical therapies.","requirements":"

If you agree to have your dog participate in this study, the following procedures will occur:

* CT scan and TACE while under anesthesia

* A second CT scan approximately 4 weeks post-TACE

* Hospitalization for 1-2 days post treatment pending response to treatment

* Completion of questionnaires

","who_can_participate":"

We are looking for dogs diagnosed with liver cancer that has been determined to be non-removable or in a location with great surgical risk.

Before your pet begins the study, your pet will need to have the following tests to find out if he/she can be in the study:


  1. Bloodwork: If bloodwork demonstrates significant disease affecting other organs, we will discuss whether your dog can be enrolled.
  2. CT Scan: A CT scan will be performed to assess tumor location and blood supply.
